ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=-2x+2$ intersects the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis at points $A$ and $B$, respectively, and the ray $AP\perp AB$ at point $A$. If point $C$ is a moving point on ray $AP$, and point $D$ is a moving point on the $x$-axis, and the triangle with vertices $C$, $D$, $A$ is congruent to $\triangle AOB$, then what is the length of $OD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In $y = -2x + 2$, \\
when $x = 0$, then $y = 2$; when $y = 0$, then $x = 1$,\\
$\therefore$ $OA = 1$, $OB = 2$, by the Pythagorean theorem we get $AB = \sqrt{OA^2 + OB^2} = \sqrt{5}$,\\
(1) When $\angle ACD = 90^\circ$, as in figure 1,\\
$\because \triangle AOB \cong \triangle DCA$,\\
$\therefore AD = AB = \sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore OD = 1 + \sqrt{5}$;\\
(2) When $\angle ADC = 90^\circ$, as in figure 2,\\
$\because AP \perp AB$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAP = \angle AOB = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABO + \angle BAO = \angle CAD + \angle BAO = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABO = \angle CAD$,\\
$\because \triangle AOB \cong \triangle CDA$,\\
$\therefore AD = OB = 2$,\\
$\therefore OA + AD = 3$,\\
In conclusion: the length of $OD$ is $1 + \sqrt{5}$ or $\boxed{3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the coordinate axes intersect at O; the oblique straight line goes from the upper left to the lower right, and intersects the positive half-axis of the y-axis at B and the positive half-axis of the x-axis at A respectively; from A there is a ray AP going toward the upper right, and in the figure it is marked near A that AP is perpendicular to the oblique line AB. Reasoning: From the line y=-2x+2, let y=0 to get x=1, so A=(1,0), OA=1; let x=0 to get y=2, so B=(0,2), OB=2. Triangle AOB is right-angled at O, so AB=sqrt(1^2+2^2)=sqrt(5). Because C is on ray AP, D is on the x-axis, and AP is not perpendicular to the x-axis, the right angle of triangle CDA cannot be at A, and can only be at C or D. Case 1: If angle ACD=90°, then in the congruent correspondence AD is the hypotenuse, corresponding to AB, so AD=sqrt(5). At this time D is on the right side of A, therefore OD=OA+AD=1+sqrt(5). Case 2: If angle ADC=90°, since AP perpendicular AB, angle BAP=90°, and also angle AOB=90°, it can be obtained that angle ABO and angle CAD correspond; when triangles AOB and CDA are congruent, AD corresponds to OB, so AD=2. At this time D is on the right side of A, OD=OA+AD=1+2=3.
